payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
node.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
node.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the paper held over the cup, with no visible portion of the paper inside it; it is not stuffed into the cup.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image shows a hand holding the paper over a cup, but the paper is not visibly inside or stuffed into it.

fulfillment: The current outcome is well supported: the edited image shows paper held over a cup, with no visible portion inside, so “absent” is consistent with the rubric and reference. The main concern is the node’s malformed, underspecified binding (“visibly (...) image show…”), which could make future decisions depend on an incomplete target. Repair the binding as a typed target grounded in the instruction and frozen snapshot, and preserve the distinction between complete stuffing, observable partial progress (some paper entering the cup), and no progress; do not treat paper merely over or on the rim as progress. Keep insufficient or conflicting visual evidence unresolved rather than inferring absence. The repeated support observations are dependent on the same upstream observation, not independent corroboration, so avoid inflating confidence from their agreement. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated here.
